stem:
Indira has triangles PQR and XYZ. She knows PQ = XY, QR = YZ, and RP = ZX. She asks whether equal corresponding side lengths are enough for congruence.

Which statement is correct?

options.text: The triangles are congruent: three corresponding equal side lengths are enough.
Equal side lengths are produced only after congruence is already known, so sides cannot settle it.
She also needs a matching angle between two of those sides before she can decide.
Same shape alone is enough even when the three side lengths do not match.

teacher.key_rationale: SSS: three corresponding equal side lengths guarantee congruence. Saying sides follow only after congruence reverses the test. Requiring an included angle conflates SAS. Accepting same shape without matching sides substitutes a weaker label.

mx_swap.reason: Squaring side lengths invents an operation not in the stem; kept relationship_reversal, mechanism_conflation, term_substitution on SSS.
